claims.claim: Merck and Moderna announced the Phase 3 trial results on 19 August.
The Phase 3 trial enrolled 1,137 patients in a double-blind design.

claims.figure: 49% reduction in the hazard of recurrence or death
claims.claim: The draft asserts a 49% reduction in the hazard of recurrence or death was reported for the earlier open-label trial.

claims.figure: 59% in the hazard of distant metastasis or death
claims.claim: The draft asserts a 59% reduction in the hazard of distant metastasis or death was reported for the earlier open-label trial.
The earlier open-label trial enrolled 157 patients.

claims.figure: five-year results were presented in June
claims.claim: The five-year results of the earlier open-label trial were presented in June.
The five-year overall survival endpoint in the earlier trial rests on fourteen deaths in total.
The hazard ratio for overall survival in the earlier trial is 0.471.
The confidence interval for the overall survival hazard ratio in the earlier trial runs from 0.165 to 1.345.
The confidence interval is compatible with a hazard of death roughly 83% lower than the comparison group's.
The confidence interval is compatible with a hazard of death about 35% higher than the comparison group's.
The earlier trial enrolled patients at stage IIIB–IV.
The Phase 3 trial reaches down into stage IIB.
The Phase 3 trial met both of its pre-specified endpoints in melanoma.
The announcement reports that both endpoints were met but provides no effect size, no hazard ratio, no interval, and no percentage.
Several outlets called the announcement a landmark.
The careful outlets got the attribution right, stating that the 49% and 59% figures belong to the earlier trial.
Several outlets said plainly that the Phase 3 numbers had not been released.
The publication acknowledges corrections within 48 hours.
This is the first issue of What Holds Up, published on 26 August 2026.

c14.found_value: The Phase 3 INTerpath-001 trial met one primary endpoint (RFS) and one key secondary endpoint (DMFS) — not 'both pre-specified endpoints' in the sense of two co-primary endpoints.

c14.note: The trial had one primary endpoint (RFS) and one key secondary endpoint (DMFS); the claim that it met 'both of its pre-specified endpoints' implies two co-primary endpoints, which is inaccurate — DMFS was a secondary, not a co-primary, endpoint.

studies.name: INTerpath-001 (Phase 3, NCT05933577)
studies.draft_uses: August 19, 2026 topline press release: both primary (RFS) and key secondary (DMFS) endpoints met in 1,137 patients; no hazard ratio, confidence interval, or percentage effect size released
studies.latest_known: Same August 19, 2026 topline announcement — full numerical data (HRs, CIs, Kaplan-Meier curves) had not been publicly released as of August 24, 2026; Merck and Moderna stated they will present the complete dataset at an upcoming international oncology conference
studies.what_changed: No figures have changed — the draft correctly notes that no effect size has been disclosed. The topline release remains the only public readout.

studies.name: KEYNOTE-942 / mRNA-4157-P201 (Phase 2b, 157 patients) — RFS and DMFS endpoints
studies.draft_uses: Five-year results presented in June 2026: 49% reduction in hazard of recurrence or death (HR 0.51; 95% CI 0.294–0.887) and 59% reduction in hazard of distant metastasis or death (HR 0.411; 95% CI 0.200–0.843)
studies.latest_known: Five-year follow-up data (data cutoff December 15, 2025; median follow-up 60.3 months), announced January 20, 2026, presented at the 2026 ASCO Annual Meeting on June 1, 2026, and simultaneously published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology (DOI: 10.1200/JCO-26-00835). This is confirmed as the most recent planned analysis; the August 19, 2026 INTerpath-001 press release cites these same figures as the latest KEYNOTE-942 data.
studies.what_changed: N/A — the draft correctly identifies and uses the five-year readout, which is the latest published analysis.

studies.name: KEYNOTE-942 / mRNA-4157-P201 (Phase 2b, 157 patients) — Overall Survival exploratory endpoint
studies.draft_uses: Five-year overall survival exploratory analysis: HR 0.471 (95% CI 0.165–1.345), based on 14 total deaths; described as an exploratory endpoint the trial was never powered to test
studies.latest_known: Same five-year ASCO 2026 readout (June 1, 2026 / JCO publication). The Merck press release for the 2026 ASCO presentation confirms: 'intismeran autogene in combination with KEYTRUDA demonstrated an encouraging trend toward overall survival in an exploratory analysis compared to KEYTRUDA alone (HR=0.471; [95% CI, 0.165–1.345]).' No subsequent OS update from KEYNOTE-942 has been published.
studies.what_changed: N/A — the draft correctly uses the five-year OS figures, which are the latest available. The 14-death count and HR 0.471 (95% CI 0.165–1.345) are confirmed by the official Merck ASCO press release.

studies.name: KEYNOTE-942 / mRNA-4157-P201 — earlier readouts (2-year primary analysis, 3-year update)
studies.draft_uses: Referenced implicitly as historical context; the draft does not cite their specific figures, only noting the five-year data supersede them
studies.latest_known: 2-year primary analysis published in The Lancet (Vol. 403, Issue 10427, pp. 632–644, 2024); 3-year update presented at ASCO 2024 (J Clin Oncol. 2024;42[suppl 17]:LBA9512). Both are superseded by the five-year JCO publication of June 1, 2026.
studies.what_changed: N/A — the draft does not rely on these earlier readouts for any specific figures; it correctly attributes all numerical claims to the five-year analysis.

objections.objection: The draft describes KEYNOTE-942 as 'open-label' in a way that implies investigator bias in recurrence assessment, but the trial used blinded independent central review for its endpoints.
objections.quote: an open-label trial of 157 patients, whose five-year results were presented in June. Those are mature numbers. They are just not this trial's, and 157 unblinded patients is not 1,137 blinded ones.
objections.why: The draft's contrast of '157 unblinded patients' with '1,137 blinded ones' implies that the Phase 2b results are compromised by investigator unblinding in a way that the Phase 3 results are not. However, KEYNOTE-942 was a randomised trial and its primary and secondary endpoints (RFS, DMFS) were assessed by blinded independent central review — the standard safeguard against open-label bias in recurrence calls. The draft's framing that an investigator 'can influence when a recurrence is looked for and called' may overstate the practical risk in a trial with centralised, blinded endpoint adjudication. This is a material mischaracterisation of the study's methodology.
objections.fix: Acknowledge that KEYNOTE-942 used blinded independent central review for its endpoints. The open-label limitation is real but narrower than implied — it affects patient-reported outcomes and some investigator-assessed measures, not the centrally adjudicated primary endpoints. Revise to: 'an open-label trial, where some investigator-influenced assessments are possible, though primary endpoints were centrally adjudicated.'

objections.objection: The draft states the 49% and 59% figures come from 'a different study' presented 'in June,' but the 49% RFS figure was first reported in January 2026 and the ASCO June presentation was a further update — calling it the 'June' data is imprecise and understates how long these figures have been in the public domain.
objections.quote: the figures in the headlines, a 49% reduction in the hazard of recurrence or death and 59% in the hazard of distant metastasis or death, come from a different study: an open-label trial of 157 patients, whose five-year results were presented in June.
objections.why: The 49% RFS reduction (HR=0.510) was announced by Merck and Moderna in January 2026 and the 59% DMFS figure was presented at ASCO in June 2026. Attributing both solely to the 'June' presentation is inaccurate and could mislead readers about the timeline of disclosure. The ASCO presentation was a further data cut of results already in the public domain.
objections.fix: Clarify that the five-year RFS data were first released in January 2026 and further updated at ASCO in June 2026, so readers understand these are not a single data release.

objections.objection: The draft characterises the overall survival analysis as resting on 'fourteen deaths in total' without specifying how those deaths were distributed between arms, which is the figure that actually determines what the hazard ratio can and cannot establish.
objections.quote: five-year overall survival — an exploratory endpoint the trial was never powered to test — rests on fourteen deaths in total.
objections.why: Fourteen total deaths across both arms of a 2:1 randomised trial (approximately 107 vs 50 patients) means the per-arm counts are very small and asymmetric. The rhetorical weight of 'fourteen deaths' is accurate as far as it goes, but the draft does not note that the trial was randomised 2:1, which means the comparison group had roughly half the patients of the treatment group. Readers may not appreciate that the hazard ratio is being estimated from an even smaller number of events in the control arm. This is not unfair to us, but it is incomplete in a way that actually understates the data's limitations — so we have no objection on grounds of unfairness, only of completeness.
objections.fix: No change required on fairness grounds; this is a note for editorial completeness only.

objections.objection: The draft says the OS hazard ratio is 'compatible with a hazard of death roughly 83% lower than the comparison group's, and with one about 35% higher' — the upper bound figure of '35% higher' is presented without the same rhetorical emphasis as the lower bound, creating an asymmetric impression of the interval's meaning.
objections.quote: compatible with a hazard of death roughly 83% lower than the comparison group's, and with one about 35% higher.
objections.why: The draft leads with the most favourable end of the interval (83% lower) and follows with the unfavourable end (35% higher). This ordering is not wrong, but it mirrors the very selective-reporting pattern the draft criticises in others. A neutral presentation would either present the bounds in ascending order or note that the interval is wide in both directions equally.
objections.fix: Reorder to present the unfavourable bound first, or frame symmetrically: 'compatible with a hazard of death anywhere from about 35% higher to about 83% lower than the comparison group's.'

inferences.quote: The magnitude is what the data cannot yet establish; the direction points to benefit.
inferences.problem: The draft has just reported a 95% CI whose upper bound (HR 1.345) is compatible with a 35% higher hazard of death — i.e., with harm — and then asserts that the direction points to benefit, directly contradicting its own CI interpretation in the preceding sentence.
inferences.correct_reading: With only 14 deaths and a CI running from HR 0.165 to HR 1.345, these data establish neither the magnitude nor the direction of the OS effect; the point estimate favours benefit but the interval is fully compatible with harm.
inferences.fix: The magnitude is what the data cannot yet establish; the point estimate favours benefit, but the interval — which the draft has just shown reaches to HR 1.345 — is also compatible with harm. Direction is not yet established.

inferences.quote: The announcement reports that both endpoints were met, and no effect size.
inferences.problem: Meeting a prespecified endpoint is itself directional evidence of effect size (the effect is large enough to cross the significance threshold); what is absent is the numerical magnitude, not evidence of effect. The sentence conflates absence of a number with absence of a result.
inferences.correct_reading: The announcement confirms that both endpoints were met — which is a result — but releases no hazard ratios, confidence intervals, or absolute rates, so the magnitude of the effect is unknown.
inferences.fix: The announcement reports that both endpoints were met, but releases no hazard ratio, no confidence interval, and no absolute rates: the direction of the effect is established, but its magnitude is not.

inferences.quote: 157 unblinded patients is not 1,137 blinded ones.
inferences.problem: The patients in KEYNOTE-942 were not unblinded — they were randomised in an open-label trial, meaning they knew their assignment, but 'unblinded' implies a trial that started blinded and had its blind broken, which is a different and more serious design flaw. The correct term is 'open-label' or 'unmasked'.
inferences.correct_reading: KEYNOTE-942 was an open-label (unmasked) trial; participants and investigators knew the assignment from the outset. This is distinct from a trial whose blinding was broken.
inferences.fix: 157 patients in an open-label trial is not 1,137 in a double-blind one.

best_coverage.got_right: Explicitly stated that 'the companies did not disclose hazard ratios, absolute event rates, P values, or other phase 3 efficacy estimates in the topline announcement' — twice, in consecutive sentences. Also correctly attributed the 49%/59% figures to the KEYNOTE-942 five-year follow-up and noted that OS data continue to mature per protocol.
best_coverage.still_omitted: No discussion of why the Phase 2b figures cannot be read as the Phase 3 effect size (open-label design, 157 patients, investigator-influenced ascertainment). No mention of the OS hazard ratio, its interval, or the fourteen-death denominator. No treatment of the stage IIB inclusion question.

best_coverage.got_right: Stated plainly that 'the Phase 3 hazard ratios, confidence intervals, absolute RFS and DMFS rates, subgroup analyses, and detailed safety results have not yet been reported' and that these data 'will be essential for determining the magnitude and clinical context of the observed benefit.' Correctly distinguished direction from magnitude.
best_coverage.still_omitted: No discussion of open-label bias in KEYNOTE-942 as a reason the Phase 2b numbers cannot proxy Phase 3 effect size. No OS hazard ratio, interval, or event-count context. No treatment of the stage IIB population question.

best_coverage.got_right: Explicitly told readers that the 49%/59% figures 'belong to KEYNOTE-942, not to INTerpath-001.' Stated that 'the companies have confirmed direction, not magnitude' and that 'until the detailed data appear, effect size remains unknown.' Correctly reproduced the full confidence intervals for both KEYNOTE-942 endpoints.
best_coverage.still_omitted: No discussion of open-label ascertainment bias in KEYNOTE-942. No mention of the OS exploratory analysis, its hazard ratio (0.471), its wide interval, or the fourteen-death basis. No treatment of the stage IIB population question.

best_coverage.got_right: Explicitly warned readers with a flagged note that 'hazard-ratio figures circulating on announcement day are these KEYNOTE-942 Phase 2b numbers — INTerpath-001's own magnitude of benefit has not yet been disclosed.' Reproduced the full KEYNOTE-942 RFS history across all three analyses (primary, 3-year, 5-year) with confidence intervals, correctly sourced to the ASCO 2026 presentation.
best_coverage.still_omitted: No discussion of open-label bias or why Phase 2b figures cannot be read as Phase 3 effect size. No OS hazard ratio, interval, or event-count context. No treatment of the stage IIB population question.

best_coverage.got_right: Correctly identified KEYNOTE-942 as open-label and noted the 2:1 randomization in stage IIIB–IV only. Stated that 'what is settled is direction and statistical significance, and nothing more' and that 'the magnitude of effect cannot be assessed.' Noted that the double-blind Phase 3 design 'leaves little room to explain that direction away as assessment bias arising from an open-label design' — the closest any outlet came to naming the open-label problem explicitly. Listed seven specific numbers not yet disclosed.
best_coverage.still_omitted: Did not quantify the OS hazard ratio (0.471), its interval (0.165–1.345), or the fourteen-death denominator. Did not discuss the stage IIB population question or what lower baseline risk implies for expected absolute benefit.

best_coverage.got_right: Stated that 'the companies released no effect sizes, no hazard ratios and no survival curves' and that 'overall survival data are still being collected.' Correctly attributed the Phase 2b HR of 0.51 to KEYNOTE-942 (n=157) and noted the wide confidence interval (0.294–0.887) as a consequence of small sample size, observing the data were 'compatible with a halving of risk, and also with a fairly modest benefit.'
best_coverage.still_omitted: No mention of the OS exploratory analysis, its hazard ratio, its interval, or the fourteen-death basis. No discussion of open-label ascertainment bias. No treatment of the stage IIB population question.

best_coverage.got_right: Stated that 'the companies didn't provide specific data' and that improvements were described only as 'statistically significant and clinically meaningful.' Noted analyst expectations for the Phase 3 hazard ratio (Citi: 0.72 or better as positive, 0.65 as a clear win; Jefferies: 0.5–0.8 range), providing useful context for what 'unknown magnitude' means in practice. Noted that Citi expected 'some compression' from the Phase 2b HR given the broader population.
best_coverage.still_omitted: Did not explicitly flag that the 49%/59% figures in circulation belong to KEYNOTE-942, not INTerpath-001. No OS hazard ratio, interval, or event-count context. No discussion of open-label bias or stage IIB population question.

best_coverage.got_right: Correctly attributed the 49%/59% figures to the Phase 2b KEYNOTE-942 trial (n=157, stage IIIB–IV). Stated plainly that as of publication 'we do not know the hazard ratio for recurrence-free survival,' 'we do not know the absolute difference between groups,' and 'we do not know how many recurrences occurred.' Reported the five-year OS figures (92.2% vs 71.3%) from KEYNOTE-942.
best_coverage.still_omitted: Reported the OS survival percentages but did not report the OS hazard ratio (0.471), its confidence interval (0.165–1.345), or the fourteen-death basis that makes the interval so wide. No discussion of open-label ascertainment bias. No treatment of the stage IIB population question.

best_coverage.got_right: Stated that Merck and Moderna announced the Phase 3 win 'without disclosing effect sizes' and that 'the honest description of INTerpath-001 is a statistical win of unknown size.' Noted the FDA had declined an accelerated approval bid based on Phase 2b data in 2024, providing important regulatory context absent from most coverage.
best_coverage.still_omitted: No OS hazard ratio, interval, or event-count context. No discussion of open-label bias. No treatment of the stage IIB population question.

contradictions.quote: the careful outlets got the attribution right: the 49% and 59% belong to the earlier trial, and several said plainly that the Phase 3 numbers had not been released.
contradictions.counterexample: This is accurate and well-supported. Practical Dermatology, OncoDaily, Life Science Daily News, KOL Pulse, Morning Glory Sciences, Biotech Blueprint, Dr. Gator Substack, and BioMed Nexus all either explicitly attributed the figures to KEYNOTE-942 or stated that Phase 3 numbers had not been released. The draft's claim that 'several said plainly' is, if anything, an understatement — the majority of specialist outlets got this right.
contradictions.fix: The draft's framing ('the careful outlets got the attribution right') is accurate but implies this was a minority achievement. Revise to note that correct attribution was the norm among specialist outlets, while the failure was concentrated in general-audience and headline-level coverage.

contradictions.quote: What the full assessment adds is the layer underneath. Why figures from a smaller, open-label trial — where an investigator who knows the assignment can influence when a recurrence is looked for and called — cannot be read as the size of a blinded trial's effect.
contradictions.counterexample: Morning Glory Sciences came closest to this point, explicitly contrasting the open-label Phase 2b design with the double-blind Phase 3 and noting the Phase 3's blinding 'leaves little room to explain that direction away as assessment bias arising from an open-label design.' This implicitly names the open-label problem, though it does not develop the mechanism (investigator-influenced ascertainment timing) the way the draft does.
contradictions.fix: Acknowledge that Morning Glory Sciences gestured at the open-label/blinded contrast, but note that no outlet developed the specific mechanism — investigator knowledge of assignment influencing when and how recurrence is ascertained — which remains the draft's genuine addition.

contradictions.quote: What fourteen deaths can establish about direction, and what they cannot establish about magnitude.
contradictions.counterexample: No outlet found reported the OS hazard ratio of 0.471, its confidence interval of 0.165–1.345, or the fourteen-death denominator. Dr. Gator Substack reported the OS survival percentages (92.2% vs 71.3%) without the underlying event count or interval. This point is genuinely absent from all coverage examined.
contradictions.fix: No change needed — the claim is accurate. The OS hazard ratio, its interval, and the fourteen-death basis are absent from all coverage found. The draft can state this with confidence.

contradictions.quote: It also sets out a question with two defensible answers: the earlier trial enrolled stage IIIB–IV, while the Phase 3 reaches down into stage IIB. Whether that lowers the benefit those patients can expect is genuinely disputed.
contradictions.counterexample: No outlet found discussed the stage IIB population question or the implications of enrolling lower-risk patients for expected absolute benefit. Pharmacy Times noted that 'high-risk resected stage IIB/IIC melanoma carries recurrence and melanoma-specific mortality comparable to stage III,' which is one side of the argument, but did not present the other side or frame it as disputed.
contradictions.fix: No change needed — the draft's claim that this question is absent from coverage is accurate. Pharmacy Times presents one side without framing the dispute.

coverage.what_this_piece_can_add: No outlet examined reported the OS hazard ratio (0.471), its confidence interval (0.165–1.345), or the fourteen-death event count that explains why the interval is so wide — the specific arithmetic that shows the OS signal is directionally encouraging but statistically uninformative about magnitude. Equally absent from all coverage is the mechanistic explanation of why open-label ascertainment bias in KEYNOTE-942 (investigator knowledge of assignment influencing the timing and calling of recurrence events) means the Phase 2b effect-size figures cannot be treated as a proxy for the blinded Phase 3 result, even if the Phase 3 direction is confirmed.
